title: AKS Diagnostics and Errors

controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.34 search returns zero rows.

description: Control plane and node problems surface as API errors, failed mounts, and ImagePullBackOff; centralized errors shorten MTTR.
value: Detecting aks diagnostics and errors early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable AKS diagnostic categories for audit and container logs. Ingest to Splunk. Alert on elevated 5xx from API server or repeated ImagePullBackOff patterns. Dashboard by namespace and deployment.
visualization: Table (resource, code, count), Timeline (audit errors), Bar chart (namespace).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable AKS diagnostic categories for audit and container logs. Ingest to Splunk. Alert on elevated 5xx from API server or repeated ImagePullBackOff patterns. Dashboard by namespace and deployment.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" category="kube-audit" "responseStatus.code">=400
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.34_aks_diagnostics_and_erro_34"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect aks diagnostics and errors. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_34_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (resource, code, count), Timeline (audit errors), Bar chart (namespace)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aks diagnostics and errors so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
